rules.rule: Test defects only: mocks or stubs that hide integration defects or bypass the real authority path; regression behavior not actually exercised (missing assertions, assertions trivially true); tests coupled to implementation details instead of observable behavior; tests duplicating production logic instead of exercising the real path; guard/wiring tests weakened or removed to make a change pass; e2e specs that cannot detect the failure they claim to cover.

Content/registry defects only: duplicate IDs; references to non-existent IDs; inconsistent relationships between content entries; dependency-direction violations (data files importing runtime systems); content definitions embedding runtime authority that belongs in systems; authored effects or flags the engine cannot execute (silent-downgrade risk); content changes without a matching mechanic on the consuming side.

Phaser/scene defects only: duplicate scene-transition authority; incorrect scene lifecycle use (init/preload/create/update/shutdown); double initialization; event listeners registered more than once or never removed; tweens/timers/textures/objects not released on shutdown or destroy; assets loaded by the wrong owner; one scene directly controlling unrelated scenes; transition race conditions; authoritative gameplay state mutated from render or animation code.

Vue/Pinia defects only: UI owning domain logic or computing authoritative gameplay results; direct domain-state mutation from presentation instead of owner APIs; duplicated reactive authority over one piece of state; stale reactive state after reset/restore; incorrect watchers (missing immediate/deep/flush needs, watch loops); missing cleanup in onUnmounted/onScopeDispose; event-listener, timer, or subscription leaks; Vue-Pinia-Phaser synchronization errors; hardcoded UI strings bypassing the i18n gateway; computed/ref misuse causing stale or lost reactivity.

Domain/combat authority defects only: logic bypassing the owning system's API; direct mutation of another system's state; multiple sources of truth for one rule or state; invalid or duplicated state transitions; damage/vitals resolution outside the gameplay authority; duplicated formulas or calculations across systems; buff/debuff lifecycle errors (double-apply, missing expiry, wrong owner); hidden side effects inside queries or previews; nondeterministic combat outcomes from shared mutable state; missing cleanup on reset/restore; one-shot effects executing more than once; orchestrators reimplementing domain rules instead of delegating.

Service/orchestration defects only: orchestrators reimplementing domain rules instead of delegating to owners; swallowed errors that leave callers believing an operation succeeded; async work without a lifecycle owner, cleanup, or stale-result policy; overlapping sessions without identity/generation checks; partial failures reported as full success.
